title: DevEx Documentation Playbook: SDK Guides, Quickstarts, API Examples, Docs Ops & Canonical Fixes
author: Maya Thompson
body:
Summary:
This playbook documents the standards, templates, and operational procedures for Developer Experience (DevEx) content: SDK guides, quickstarts and templates, canonical API examples, docs-site operations, and the canonical fixes for recurring support issues. It is the source of truth for authors and on-call support.

Audience:
- DevEx writers and engineers
- Solutions engineers preparing customer examples
- On-call support and tech writers maintaining the docs site

Goals:
- Consistent SDK guides and quickstarts across languages
- 5-10 minute runnable quickstarts for first-success moments
- Robust docs-site ops with CI smoke tests and rollback procedures
- Canonical troubleshooting steps for top support issues to reduce MTTR

Ownership & SLAs:
- Content owner: DevEx (engineering)
- Primary on-call: DevEx writer (monthly rotation)
- Reviewers: API SDK owners and Security
- SLA: Critical docs updated within 3 business days; routine edits within 10 business days

Required structure for every SDK guide (section checklist):
1) Title and short purpose (1 sentence)
2) Compatibility matrix (SDK version -> API version)
3) Quickstart (runnable in <=10 minutes)
4) Auth & config examples (env, CLI, KMS notes)
5) Common patterns & idioms (batching, streaming, error handling)
6) Troubleshooting & links to canonical fixes
7) API reference links & changelog notes
8) Ownership and last-reviewed date

Docs-site operating procedures (ops playbook):
- Merge & deploy cadence:
  1. Author opens PR against docs/main (assign DevEx + API owner).
  2. CI pipeline: lint -> build -> link-check -> staging deploy.
  3. Staging smoke tests must pass before promoting to prod.
  4. Production deploy window: daily 02:00 UTC; emergency hotfixes allowed with on-call approval.

- Staging smoke checklist (CI or manual):
  - Home page renders with no console errors
  - Top nav links return 200
  - Canonical Python quickstart runs inside disposable container CI job
  - Search index is updated and returns expected top results for sample queries

- Rollback policy:
  - If prod deploy causes regression, revert to previous build, open incident, and notify #devex-docs and impacted PO(s).

Quickstart template (copyable):
- 1-line purpose
- Prerequisites (OS, runtimes, API key scope)
- Install instructions
- Minimal example (save-and-run)
- Run command(s) and expected output sample
- Next steps & links to API reference
- Security notice about secrets

Example: Python quickstart (minimal)
Prerequisites:
- Python 3.9+
- REDWOOD_API_KEY with developer scope

Install:
- pip install redwood-sdk

Example (quickstart.py):
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key="${REDWOOD_API_KEY}")
resp = client.generate("Write a friendly subject line for the Q1 report")
print(resp.text)

Run:
REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-xxx python quickstart.py

Example: Node quickstart (minimal)
Prerequisites: Node 18+
Install: npm install @redwood/inference
Example (index.mjs):
import Redwood from '@redwood/inference';
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
const resp = await client.generate('Summarize meeting notes in two bullets.');
console.log(resp.text);

cURL quick API check:
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-1.0","prompt":"Translate to French: Hello world"}'

Auth and secrets guidance:
- Prefer environment variables for local quickstarts (REDWOOD_API_KEY).
- For production, reference KMS/HSM: fetch keys from customer KMS and inject via env/secret mount.
- Do not store long-lived secrets in sample repos; include a security notice at repo top.

Compatibility matrix (required):
| SDK | Version | API | Notes |
| python | 0.8.x | v1 | streaming beta supported |
| node | 0.7.x | v1 | function-calling examples included |
| go | 0.3.x | v1 | batching primitives experimental |

Canonical API examples to include in SDK docs:
- Streaming text generation (Python + curl)
- Function / tool calling (Node + JSON schema)
- Embeddings: single vs batch patterns and rate-limit notes

Streaming example (Python):
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key="${REDWOOD_API_KEY}")
for chunk in client.stream_generate("Explain Newton's first law in simple terms"):
  print(chunk, end='')

Top support issues and canonical fixes (triage-first):
1) API returns 401 in CI jobs
   - Symptom: Works locally; CI shows 401
   - Cause: Secret not injected or masked in CI environment
   - Fix: Verify secret injection in CI logs, ensure variable REDWOOD_API_KEY exists in job env, rotate key if compromised. Add CI snippet to quickstart.

2) Streaming stalls after initial tokens
   - Symptom: stream_generate yields a few chunks then stalls
   - Cause: Network proxy or HTTP client buffering; using sync API with streaming expectation
   - Fix: Use streaming-compatible HTTP client config in SDK guide, test with curl --no-buffer, document proxy bypass and telemetry flags.

3) Embeddings slow or 429 during bulk runs
   - Symptom: High latency or 429s on embedding jobs
   - Cause: Per-second rate-limits or non-batched calls
   - Fix: Use batch_embeddings endpoint, implement exponential backoff with full jitter; example params: max_retries=5, base_delay=0.5s.

4) Unexpected generation style (model mismatch)
   - Symptom: Output tone/style differs from expectation
   - Cause: Client pinned to older model or routed to fallback variant
   - Fix: Link to compatibility matrix and show how to pin model_version in request (e.g., model: "redwood-1.1").

Canonical fix snippets (GitHub Actions secret injection):
env:
  REDWOOD_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.REDWOOD_API_KEY }}

Publish checklist for new quickstarts:
- Title & short purpose
- Verified run time < 10 minutes in CI
- Minimal example runnable (CI smoke job)
- Security note on secrets
- Compatibility matrix present
- Reviewed by API owner and security reviewer
- Labels: language tag, quickstart, tutorial

Publishing & review flow:
1) Open PR against docs/main; assign DevEx + API owner reviewers
2) CI smoke tests run; fix failures
3) If SDK/API impact, mark as in_review for 48 hours for SDK team feedback
4) Merge after approvals; CI deploy to staging; run staging quickstart verification if required
5) Schedule production deploy in next window or request hotfix

Docs health metrics (tracked weekly):
- Docs site uptime target: 99.9%
- Search success rate (top 50 queries) target: 95%
- Quickstart CI smoke job success: 100% for canonical job
- Average TTFB for docs pages: < 500ms

On-call & escalation:
- CI failures blocking publishing: page DevEx on-call; open Jira P2
- Production site outages: page eng-sre and follow incident runbook

Related resources:
- developer-experience-docs-operating-procedures-2026.json
- developer-experience-sdk-quickstarts-and-api-examples-2026.json
- Internal API reference: /confluence/eng-developer-experience/api-examples

Appendix: Backoff pseudo-code:
def backoff(attempt):
  return base_delay * (2 ** attempt) + random.uniform(0, jitter)
